lessons.title: Agents
lessons.summary: Understand agents by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Control patterns
paragraphs: Workflow: Application code fixes the execution path.
Agent: A model dynamically selects actions within constraints.
Tool: An external capability supplies observations or effects.
Environment: The external state supplies feedback to the acting system.

sections.title: Reasoning loop
paragraphs: Plan: Propose steps toward the goal.
Act: Invoke an authorized capability.
Observe: Inspect actual execution feedback.
Respond: Give a final user-facing outcome.

sections.title: State
paragraphs: Working state: Holds intermediate task data during execution.
Persistent memory: Retains selected information beyond one run.
Conversation history: Preserves dialogue needed to interpret requests.
External record: A trusted system owns authoritative business data.

sections.title: Boundaries
paragraphs: Permission: Limits what actions the agent may perform.
Budget: Limits execution time, rounds or cost.
Approval: Requires an authorized decision for consequential actions.
Isolation: Contains execution and limits access to unrelated resources.

sections.title: Reliability
paragraphs: Task evaluation: Measure success on representative cases.
Trace review: Inspect the actual sequence of model and tool events.
Fallback: Use a simpler supported path when agent execution fails.
Honest outcome: Report unresolved work instead of claiming completion.

lessons.title: Tool Calling
lessons.summary: Understand tool calling by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Discovery
paragraphs: Name: Identifies a registered capability.
Description: Explains when and why a tool should be used.
Argument schema: Defines permitted input structure.
Availability: Determines which capabilities are exposed in this run.

sections.title: Execution
paragraphs: Validation: Reject malformed or semantically invalid arguments.
Authorization: Check rights independently of model output.
Dispatch: Invoke registered host code after checks.
Observation: Return the real execution result.

sections.title: Parallel operations
paragraphs: Independent calls: May execute concurrently when their effects do not conflict.
Dependent calls: Must wait for an earlier result they consume.
Correlation ID: Matches each returned observation to its request.
Concurrency limit: Bounds simultaneous operations to protect resources.

sections.title: External effects
paragraphs: Idempotency: Deduplicates repeated logical operations.
Confirmation: Obtains authorization before consequential unapproved effects.
Read-only mode: Permits observation without intended state modification.
Audit trail: Records what actually happened for later review.

sections.title: Returned content
paragraphs: Typed result: Use a documented structured output contract.
Error result: Represent unsuccessful execution explicitly.
Untrusted data: Tool content cannot override privileged instructions.
Size bound: Limit observations before adding them to context.

lessons.summary: Understand model context protocol (mcp) by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Host: An application coordinates model interaction and connected clients.
Client: Maintains a protocol connection to a server.
Server: Exposes capabilities through the protocol.
Transport: Carries protocol messages between participants.

sections.title: Primitives
paragraphs: Tool: A callable capability can retrieve information or perform an action.
Resource: Exposes contextual data identified by the server.
Prompt: A reusable interaction template is supplied by the server.
Capability negotiation: Participants advertise supported features during initialization.

sections.title: Lifecycle
paragraphs: Initialization: Establish protocol compatibility and negotiated capabilities.
Discovery: List exposed tools or other supported primitives.
Invocation: Call an available capability with validated arguments.
Disconnection: Release the connection and associated local resources.

sections.title: Security
paragraphs: Host policy: The application enforces user intent and permissions.
Server trust: Assess the source and privileges of a connected server.
Data boundary: Returned content remains untrusted input.
Credential handling: Keep credentials scoped and avoid exposing secrets.

sections.title: Interoperability
paragraphs: Schema contract: Documented argument/result formats enable correct consumption.
Version compatibility: Supported protocol revisions must be handled explicitly.
Error handling: Report protocol and operation failures without false success.
Protocol boundary: A connection standard does not guarantee tool quality or model accuracy.

sections.title: Building blocks
paragraphs: Model interface: Provides access to a chosen model through a documented abstraction.
Tool: Wraps a capability with its input contract.
Message: Represents role-labelled conversational content.
Retriever: Returns relevant documents for a query.

sections.title: Responsibility boundaries
paragraphs: Application policy: Enforces permissions and authorized behavior.
Framework abstraction: Coordinates supported components but does not guarantee correctness.
Provider contract: Determines actual model/service capabilities and limits.
Content evaluation: Checks whether outputs satisfy the task.

sections.title: Retrieval composition
paragraphs: Loader: Reads source content into document records.
Splitter: Divides source text into retrievable units.
Embedding integration: Computes representations using a selected encoder.
Vector store: Stores and searches numerical representations with associated content.

sections.title: Execution concerns
paragraphs: Structured result: Validate returned objects against an expected schema.
Streaming: Consume incremental output using supported event handling.
Cancellation: Stop obsolete work and release resources.
Tracing: Record execution events to investigate component behavior.

sections.title: Maintenance
paragraphs: Pinned dependency: Record a tested library version.
Integration test: Verify interactions with actual component contracts.
Migration review: Assess documented changes before updating code.
Minimal baseline: Compare framework composition with a simpler solution.

sections.title: Graph structure
paragraphs: Node: Performs a computation or action within a graph.
Edge: Defines a transition between nodes.
State: Carries shared execution data according to its schema.
Conditional routing: Selects a next path based on state or a decision.

sections.title: Persistence
paragraphs: Checkpoint: Captures execution state at a persistence boundary.
Thread identity: Distinguishes independent persisted execution histories.
Resume: Continues from an appropriate saved state.
State inspection: Reads persisted execution data for review.

sections.title: Human decisions
paragraphs: Interrupt: Pauses execution for external input or a decision.
Approval: An authorized person permits a proposed effect.
Edit: An authorized person changes intermediate state.
Rejection: Declines the proposed action and directs recovery.

sections.title: Concurrency
paragraphs: Reducer: Combines updates to shared state under a declared rule.
Parallel branch: Executes independent paths concurrently.
Join: Combines progress when required branches finish.
Race prevention: Avoid incompatible effects or conflicting updates.

sections.title: Durable execution
paragraphs: Idempotency: Repeated execution must not duplicate logical side effects.
Replay awareness: A recovered run may revisit computation boundaries.
Execution limit: Bound graph steps, time and cost.
Failure visibility: Expose errors without treating a checkpoint as proof of task success.

lessons.title: Workflows
lessons.summary: Understand workflows by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Patterns
paragraphs: Sequence: Runs steps in a defined order.
Routing: Chooses a specialized path for an input.
Parallelism: Runs independent work concurrently.
Evaluator loop: Uses feedback to improve or reject an intermediate output.

sections.title: Contracts
paragraphs: Precondition: States what must hold before a step runs.
Postcondition: States what a successful step guarantees.
Schema: Defines the structure of exchanged data.
Invariant: Must remain true across the workflow.

sections.title: Failure policies
paragraphs: Retry: Repeat eligible transient work under a bounded policy.
Compensation: Perform a business-level reversal of a completed effect.
Timeout: Bound waiting for a step.
Escalation: Transfer unresolved work to an authorized operator or supported fallback.

sections.title: Execution records
paragraphs: Correlation ID: Connects events belonging to one logical execution.
Checkpoint: Persists recoverable progress.
Audit event: Records consequential actions and decisions.
Metric: Aggregates behavior such as duration or failure counts.

sections.title: Design tradeoffs
paragraphs: Deterministic path: Provides explicit predictable control for known processes.
Dynamic agent: Chooses actions when the path cannot be fixed usefully.
Minimal composition: Avoid unnecessary steps and dependencies.
Representative evaluation: Tests the design on actual success criteria.

lessons.summary: Understand agent-to-agent (a2a) by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Entities
paragraphs: Agent card: Describes an agent's identity and advertised capabilities.
Task: Represents work with a lifecycle rather than just a chat string.
Message: Carries conversational content exchanged between participants.
Artifact: Represents an output produced by task execution.

sections.title: Lifecycle
paragraphs: Submitted: Work has been accepted for processing.
Working: Execution is in progress.
Input required: Execution needs further information or a decision.
Completed: Execution has finished successfully under its reported contract.

sections.title: Boundaries
paragraphs: A2A interaction: Coordinates tasks between participating agents.
Tool access: Invokes a narrower capability through an appropriate tool interface.
Internal architecture: Remains an implementation choice behind an agent endpoint.
Application authorization: Controls who may delegate or perform consequential work.

sections.title: Asynchronous behavior
paragraphs: Status update: Reports progress or a lifecycle change.
Cancellation request: Asks to stop work but must account for already completed effects.
Polling: Checks task state through repeated bounded requests.
Streaming: Receives supported incremental events over an active interaction.

sections.title: Reliability and trust
paragraphs: Identity verification: Establish that the peer is the intended service.
Capability verification: Check advertised functionality against required task needs.
Result validation: Evaluate returned artifacts before relying on them.
Protocol compatibility: Use supported message and lifecycle contracts.
